html:
SMTO-SCH-0012 — This part of a saved schedule can't be changed

GUID: 9f1ebc95-b199-4ddf-958f-50d1317f4b87
Slug: schedule-authority-immutable
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to change where or with what permissions a saved schedule runs. Those choices are fixed when a schedule is created, so nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open a conversation set up the way you want, for example using the right Gateway, and ask SMTO to create a new schedule there. A schedule keeps the computer and permissions from the conversation it was created in.
  2. Open Schedules and check that the new schedule shows the next run you expect. This confirms the replacement is ready before you stop the old one.
  3. Pause or delete the old schedule on the Schedules page. Otherwise both schedules would run the same work.
  4. For simple changes, such as the time, repeat or prompt text, select Edit on the schedule instead. Those parts can still be changed on an existing schedule.

What success looks like

  • The new schedule appears on the Schedules page with the right settings and the old one is paused or gone.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't try to work around this by editing saved files by hand.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A native (Schedule Skill) schedule update included fields outside EDITABLE_FIELDS, such as captured execution scope, Gateway target, permissions or approval settings, which edits must not modify.

What this means

  • A native schedule update contains fields outside the explicit EDITABLE_FIELDS allowlist. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • A native schedule update contains fields outside the explicit EDITABLE_FIELDS allowlist.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact unsupported field and its ownership instead of weakening the edit allowlist.

How to fix it

  • Through the Schedule Skill, only title, prompt, status, schedule_type, interval_seconds, timezone, next_run_at, recurrence, action_type, notification_message and notify_on are editable. To change target, scope or permission settings, create a new schedule from a conversation with the intended settings and pause or delete the old one; do not rewrite the saved execution authority.
  • Create a new schedule with the intended authorized target and policies. Do not rewrite the saved execution authority.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported edit preserves authority, or a new intended schedule captures changed authorized scope.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
